newsitem.title: USA: US says general's firing confirms Mexico corruption.
newsitem.headline: US says general's firing confirms Mexico corruption.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday that the firing of Mexico's top anti-drug official confirmed a pervasive problem of corruption at high levels of the Mexican government.

Mexico announced late on Tuesday that it had dismissed Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, head of its National Institute for the Combat of Drugs (INCD), for alleged links to a powerful narcotics trafficker and charged him with drug corruption.

"The firing of the Mexican drug czar ... confirms something that is fairly well known, which is that corruption has reached serious levels in the Mexican government," State Department spokesman Glynn Davies told reporters.
"It's sad and troubling," he added. "That said, we welcome (Mexican President Ernesto) Zedillo government's efforts to redress such instances of corruption".

Davies said that Rebollo's ouster had not shocked the United States, even though the White House's own drug czar had frequently praised the Mexican general as an honest commander since he took charge of the INCD in December.
U.S. National Drug Policy director Gen. Barry McCaffrey issued a statement late on Tuesday in which expressed his extreme disappointment at the turn of events in Mexico.
"This demonstrates that Mexico is seriously threatened by corruption and violence but will take strong steps to root them out," said McCaffrey, who is currently touring northwestern cities.

President Bill Clinton will have to grade Mexico and 31 other countries at the end of this month in the annual "certification" process, Washington's evaluation of how other governments fight against drugs.
Countries failing the test are open to U.S. economic and trade sanctions.
Davies declined to comment on how the case of Gutierrez might influence Mexico's certification, which is due to be announced along with decisions on other countries on Feb 27.
